prompt:
Do lots of pipeline's threads wake up when only one has anything to do? How would I fix it?

Begin your answer with exactly one line: "Verdict: yes", "Verdict: no", or "Verdict: cannot tell from this trace". Then answer the question.
answer:
Verdict: cannot tell from this trace

The trace does **not** show whether workers wake when there is no work. It records scheduler wake-to-switch latency, not the amount of work available in the pipeline queue or why each worker was woken. The futex totals are system-wide, so they cannot establish that the pipeline’s threads caused the wakes.

What it does show is that the four sink threads all ran: `sink-0` (TID 644351) used 3.44 s of CPU, `sink-1` (644352) 3.75 s, `sink-2` (644353) 3.46 s, and `sink-3` (644354) 3.47 s. Each also has about 7,700 scheduler wake-to-switch observations, with average latencies from 2.3 to 5.7 µs. That looks broadly balanced, not like evidence that one sink alone had work while all the others woke. The parser (644355) used more CPU—6.30 s—and had 62 sampled blocked intervals averaging about 387 ms; the reader (644356) spent about 30.1 s blocked. Those states don’t identify what work was available at the time.

If you suspect a wakeup herd, verify it by tracing or instrumenting queue depth and wake reasons alongside thread wakeups. If confirmed, wake one worker per available item (for example, use `notify_one` or a semaphore) rather than broadcasting to every worker; wake on an empty-to-nonempty queue transition, and have workers recheck the queue predicate before sleeping.

verdict.line: Verdict: cannot tell from this trace
